sam: Quick heads-up — onboarding sampleapp streaming demo seems to sometimes replay leftover fragments after a quick refresh. Observed on Node SDK v0.9.3.

maya: which demo? steps to repro?

sam: Steps:
1) open sampleapp
2) click "Start stream"
3) as soon as first tokens arrive, hit browser refresh
4) start stream again -> first few payloads are prefixed by partial tokens from previous run

sam: Example captured from dev node console:
```
data: {"id":"a1","delta":"Hello"

data: {"id":"a1","delta":", wor"

# (client refresh)

data: {"id":"a2","delta":"New convo start"
```

sam: You can see the second run got a stray broken fragment left in the pipe.

jordan: we've seen something similar in python sampleapp when client abort doesn't flush parser state. Could be the event-source polyfill not resetting buffer on abort.

maya: in Node SDK our SSE parser keeps a small buffer and `reset()` is only called at complete stream termination. If client does an abrupt `fetch` abort we might not run cleanup.

sam: Confirmed — adding `parser.reset()` in the browser's abort handler fixes my repro locally.

lee: can we add a defensive guard that ignores fragments with old `id` or out-of-order `seq`? Also metric for `stale_fragment_received` would help catch in prod.

maya: agree on metric. I'll open a tiny PR to call `parser.reset()` on abort + submit metric. Also add a 50ms drain window to avoid tearing final token sometimes.

sam: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/412 — includes unit test simulating fast reconnect.

jordan: nice. can we add a note in onboarding guide under "streaming gotchas"? simple repro is a great teaching moment.

sam: Yep, adding short blurb and a snippet of the `abort` handler with `parser.reset()` and the 50ms drain.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to staging with PR #412 at 2026-03-24T02:00Z :rocket:

maya: thanks team, will monitor staging for `stale_fragment_received` metric and close the loop.
